messages.subject: discrepancy between bout.metric and boutcriter
parts:
Dear Vincent,


When reviewing my results for bouted MVPA in parts 2 and 5, I realized that a discrepancy between the definitions of a bout.metric = 4 and boutcriter = 0.8 in my code creates a logical flow as only one set of bouts in either part is computed.


I therefore wondered how the code would handle this discrepancy, i.e. would bout.metric overwrite boutcriter or vice versa when computing relevant variable and therefore which definition would apply?


Part 2 variables:

AD_MVPA_E5S_B1M80%_T201_ENMO_0-24hr, AD_MVPA_E5S_B5M80%_T201_ENMO_0-24hr, AD_MVPA_E5S_B10M80%_T201_ENMO_0-24hr


Part5 variables:

dur_MVPA_D10T201_min_pla        dur_MVPA_D5T201_min_pla        dur_MVPA_D1T201_min_pla


My code is appended below.


I checked the documentation and previous posts but could not identify a similar issue.


Thank you in advance for your help.


Best,


Dominika

messages.author: 13568954e9b4ef4b
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] discrepancy between bout.metric and boutcriter
parts:
Dear Dominika,

Please note that part 2 uses arugments mvpadur and boutcriter, while part 5 uses argument boutdur.mvpa and boutcriter.mvpa. Make sure both of them are set.

Once these are set correctly the variable name in part 2 should update to the correct percentage.

I am aware that this is not very intuitive, but I have been hesitant to change argument names because that will impact on the re-usability. The price of facilitating consistency is that we are stuck with some ugly argument name choices. The same applies to some of the function names inside GGIR. At some point in the future I would like to do a clean up of the most confusing input argument names and function names, but at least not this year and not without consulting the user community.
Best wishes,
Vincent
